solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"watch" **refers to the act of observing or keeping an eye on something for a period of time.
 
• In the context of the passage, "watch" fits well as it describes the act of monitoring or guarding the coach-office for four or five hours.
 
• The other options: "clocking," "vision," and "sight" do not fit the context as appropriately.

​Therefore, the correct answer is '**Option 1**'.

**Complete Sentence:** For all that I knew this perfectly well, I still felt as if it were not safe to let the coach-office be out of my sight longer than five minutes at a time; and in this condition of unreason I had performed the first half-hour of a watch__ of four or five hours, when Wemmick ran against me.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Clocking (समय देखना/घड़ी मिलाना)**: refers to measuring or recording the time at which an event occurs.
 
• **Vision (दृष्टि)**: refers to the ability to see or a vivid mental image.
 
• **Sight (दृश्य)**: refers to the ability to see or something that is seen.
